{{ElectionsOK}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in Oklahoma''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] to represent the state of [[Oklahoma]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congressman [[Kevin Hern]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nurse N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican appointee [[Alan Armstrong]], who was named to the seat in March after [[Markwayne Mullin]] resigned to become [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of homeland security]], is prohibited by Oklahoma law from seeking a full term.

Primary elections were held on June 16. Hern, endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], won the Republican nomination with 69.8% of the vote over country singer [[Ty England]]. After no candidate received a majority in the Democratic primary, Thomas defeated attorney Jim Priest in a runoff on August 25 with 61.2% of the vote.

Democrats have not won a Senate election in Oklahoma since [[1990 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|1990]].

==Background==
A United States Senate election in Oklahoma is scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the U.S. Senate to represent the state of [[Oklahoma]]. [[Primary election]]s took place on June 16 with [[runoff election]]s on August 25 in races where no candidate received over 50 percent of the vote in June. The candidate filing deadline was April 3.<ref name="Ballotpedia">{{cite web |title=United States Senate election in Oklahoma, 2026 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Oklahoma,_2026 |website=ballotpedia.org |publisher=[[Ballotpedia]] |access-date=November 12, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> If only one candidate files for a party's nomination, they are declared the nominee.<ref>{{cite web |title=26 O.S. 6-102 |url=https://www.oscn.net/applications/oscn/DeliverDocument.asp?CiteID=78518 |website=oscn.net |publisher=[[Oklahoma State Courts Network]] |access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> 

The seat was originally held by [[Jim Inhofe]], who was last elected in [[2020 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|2020]]. Two years later, in 2022, then-Congressman [[Markwayne Mullin]] won a special election to finish Inhofe's term after Inhofe had announced his resignation at the end of the [[117th United States Congress|117th Congress]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Casteel |first1=Chris |title=Markwayne Mullin defeats Kendra Horn in Oklahoma US Senate race |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/politics/elections/state/2022/11/09/republican-markwayne-mullin-wins-race-to-replace-sen-jim-inhofe/69611629007/ |access-date=March 8, 2026 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=November 8, 2022}}</ref> After [[Donald Trump]] won the [[2024 United States presidential election]], Mullin was rumored as a contender for [[U.S. Secretary of the Interior|secretary of the interior]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Liese |first1=Sarah |last2=Hallum |first2=Katie |title=Oklahoma Sen. Markwayne Mullin reportedly in running for Trump cabinet post |url=https://www.kgou.org/politics-and-government/2024-11-12/oklahoma-sen-markwayne-mullin-reportedly-in-running-for-trump-cabinet-post |access-date=November 12, 2024 |work=[[KGOU]] |date=November 12, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Mullin's resignation would have affected the [[2026 Oklahoma gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]], as governor [[Kevin Stitt]] would have appointed a replacement who must sign a potentially unenforceable{{efn|While state law requires the appointee to sign an oath promising not to run for the following term, federal law may prevent its enforcement. The oath could lead to litigation if an appointee challenges the law.<ref name="Mullin speculation" />}} oath promising not to run for reelection in 2026.<ref name="Mullin speculation">{{cite news |last1=Savage |first1=Tres |last2=Brinkman |first2=Bennett |title=Domino scenarios: Sen. Markwayne Mullin Cabinet rumor spurs speculation |url=https://nondoc.com/2024/11/12/markwayne-mullin-cabinet-rumor-spurs-speculation/ |access-date=November 12, 2024 |work=NonDoc |date=12 November 2024}}</ref> Mullin was ultimately not nominated as the secretary of interior.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wahpekeche |first1=Dacoda |title=Sen. Markwayne Mullin talks possibly being in Donald Trump's Cabinet |url=https://www.koco.com/article/oklahoma-markwayne-mullin-donald-trump-cabinet-possibility/62910530 |access-date=November 16, 2024 |work=[[KOCO]] |date=November 15, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> However, in March 2026, Mullin was named as Trump's pick to replace [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of homeland security]] [[Kristi Noem]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Noem out, Trump picks Mullin as DHS secretary |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/05/markwayne-mullin-noem-dhs-00814761 |website=POLITICO |access-date=7 March 2026 |language=en |date=5 March 2026}}</ref> and was confirmed on March 23, 2026.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Bustillo |first=Ximena |date=2026-03-23 |title=Markwayne Mullin confirmed as the next secretary of Homeland Security |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/03/23/g-s1-114813/markwayne-mullin-confirmed-homeland-security |access-date=2026-03-24 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref>

== Interim appointment ==
Mullin was confirmed as the [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of homeland security]]<ref name=":4" /> and resigned as senator on March 23, 2026. Governor [[Kevin Stitt]] was required to appoint a replacement within 30 days. He stated the appointee would serve the remainder of the current term until January 3, 2027, though state law provides that the appointment lasts only until the November election is certified by the [[Oklahoma State Election Board]].<ref name="Oklahoman-3.7.26" /> The interim appointee must have been a registered Republican for the past five years,<ref name="shakes">{{cite web |title=Appointment of Mullin shakes up 2026 Oklahoma elections |url=https://www.kgou.org/show/capitol-insider/2026-03-06/appointment-of-mullin-shakes-up-2026-oklahoma-elections |website=KGOU NPR |access-date=8 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and they would have to sign an oath stating they will not run in the 2026 election.<ref name="NextA">{{cite web |last1=Ramos |first1=Lionel |title=Markwayne Mullin tapped to lead Homeland Security. Here's what happens to his Senate seat |url=https://www.kosu.org/whats-next-after-mullin |website=KOSU |access-date=8 March 2026 |language=en |date=5 March 2026}}</ref> On March 24, 2026, Governor Stitt announced that oil and gas executive [[Alan Armstrong]] would replace Mullin; Armstrong was sworn in by senator [[Chuck Grassley]] later that day.<ref name="PoliticoSenate">{{cite web |last=Svirnovskiy|first=Gregory|title=Stitt picks energy executive Alan Armstrong as next Oklahoma senator|url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/03/24/congress/oklahoma-senator-alan-armstrong-00841481|website=[[Politico]]|access-date=2026-03-24|language=en-US|date=2026-03-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Carney|first=Jordan|title=Introducing Sen. Alan Armstrong|url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/03/24/congress/senator-alan-armstrong-00842118|website=[[Politico]]|access-date=2026-03-24|language=en-US|date=2026-03-24}}</ref>
